construction: 153 parts in 8 root steps and three children. Steps 1–2: two floats, each two 1×16 Technic bricks with 1×8 Technic plates, stepped 2×3 and 1×3 plates and 4287a inverted slopes at the bow. Step 3: 4261 steering arms and 3651 pin connectors standing on the floats. Steps 4–8: the `Pontoon joint 1`, `2` and `3` children (a steering arm, toggle joint and axle each) and 3-long axles with half bushes forming the A-frame truss, with the 3482 rims and 3483 tyres inside the floats on 6-long axles.
interfaces: Studs up on the floats; the truss angled. The truss apex connectors meet the fuselage underside; the wheels turn on their axles inside the floats.
lesson: Twin floats for a studded Technic floatplane: each float is a pair of 1×16 Technic bricks with stepped 2×3 plates and an inverted-slope bow, carrying a wheel inside so the plane also rolls; the floats hang on a truss of 3-long axles joined by steering arms and toggle joints that set the strut angles.
parent_context: `8855 - Prop Plane.ldr` places it at (0, −0.35, 0) with the identity matrix: the floats are the lowest element, under the fuselage and ahead of the tail.
reuse_notes: Rebuild the technique: Technic-brick floats give a long slim hull with pin holes for the truss; steering arms and toggle joints let axle struts meet at non-grid angles. One joint child keeps a skewed part from the original strained model, so this is inspiration only.
